data.name: Jethian
data.gender_notes: Jethian is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Jethian comes from the Hebrew name Yithro, which means ‘he will add’ or ‘God will add’. In the Bible, Jethro is the priest of Midian who advises Moses and brings his daughter Zipporah to be his wife. As a Christian name, Jethian is a strong and meaningful choice, evoking the idea of God’s addition and support in one’s life.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies the addition of God's blessings in one's life.
data.etymology: Jethian belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God will add.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jethian total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_greek.name: Ιεθιαν
in_greek.meaning: Το νόημα του Ιεθιαν είναι δωρητής ή χορηγός
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ιεθιαν προέρχεται από τη Βίβλο και σχετίζεται με τη σημασία του 'δώρου' ή 'χορηγός'. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα συνδέεται με την έννοια της προσφοράς και της γενναιοδωρίας. Οι αρχαίοι Έλληνες και Χριστιανοί χρησιμοποιούσαν το όνομα για να εκφράσουν την ιδέα του δωρητή ή του προσφέροντος.

historical_references.reference: According to the Old Testament book of Exodus, Jethro was the priest of Midian and the father-in-law of Moses. When Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt, Jethro welcomed him and his family, and advised Moses on how to rule the people effectively, based on the principles of God's law.

In the New Testament, the name Jethro appears in the Gospel of Matthew as the name of a district or region in the area of the Sea of Galilee where Jesus performed many of his miracles. This association is not mentioned in the Old Testament, and its origin is uncertain.
